L4533: ## Including and importing the C API
L4534: 
L4535: To use the NumPy C-API you typically need to include the `numpy/ndarrayobject.h` header and `numpy/ufuncobject.h` for some ufunc related functionality (`arrayobject.h` is an alias for `ndarrayobject.h`).
L4536: These two headers export most relevant functionality. In general any project which uses the NumPy API must import NumPy using one of the functions `PyArray_ImportNumPyAPI()` or `import_array()`. In some places, functionality which requires `import_array()` is not needed, because you only need type definitions. In this case, it is sufficient to include `numpy/ndarraytypes.h`.
L4537: For the typical Python project, multiple C or C++ files will be compiled into a single shared object (the Python C-module) and `PyArray_ImportNumPyAPI()` should be called inside it's module initialization.
L4538: 
L4539: When you have a single C-file, this will consist of:
L4540: 
L4541:     #include "numpy/ndarrayobject.h"
L4542: 
L4543:     PyMODINIT_FUNC PyInit_my_module(void)
L4544:     {
L4545:         if (PyArray_ImportNumPyAPI() < 0) {
L4546:             return NULL;
L4547:         }
L4548:         /* Other initialization code. */
L4549:     }
L4550: However, most projects will have additional C files which are all linked together into a single Python module. In this case, the helper C files typically do not have a canonical place where `PyArray_ImportNumPyAPI` should be called (although it is OK and fast to call it often).
L4551: To solve this, NumPy provides the following pattern that the main file is modified to define `PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL` before the include:
L4552: 
L4553:     /* Main module file */
L4554:     #define PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL MyModule
L4555:     #include "numpy/ndarrayobject.h"
L4556: 
L4557:     PyMODINIT_FUNC PyInit_my_module(void)
L4558:     {
L4559:         if (PyArray_ImportNumPyAPI() < 0) {
L4560:             return NULL;
L4561:         }
L4562:         /* Other initialization code. */
L4563:     }
L4564: while the other files use:
L4565: 
L4566:     /* Second file without any import */
L4567:     #define NO_IMPORT_ARRAY
L4568:     #define PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL MyModule
L4569:     #include "numpy/ndarrayobject.h"
L4570: 
L4571: You can of course add the defines to a local header used throughout. You just have to make sure that the main file does _not_ define `NO_IMPORT_ARRAY`.
L4572: 
L4573: For `numpy/ufuncobject.h` the same logic applies, but the unique symbol mechanism is `#define PY_UFUNC_UNIQUE_SYMBOL` (both can match).
L4574: Additionally, you will probably wish to add a `#define NPY_NO_DEPRECATED_API NPY_1_7_API_VERSION` to avoid warnings about possible use of old API.
L4575: 
L4576: Note
L4577: 
L4578: If you are experiencing access violations make sure that the NumPy API was properly imported and the symbol `PyArray_API` is not `NULL`. When in a debugger, this symbols actual name will be `PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL``+``PyArray_API`, so for example `MyModulePyArray_API` in the above. (E.g. even a `printf("%p\n", PyArray_API);` just before the crash.)
L4579: ### Mechanism details and dynamic linking
L4580: 
L4581: The main part of the mechanism is that without NumPy needs to define a `void **PyArray_API` table for you to look up all functions. Depending on your macro setup, this takes different routes depending on whether :c:macro:`NO_IMPORT_ARRAY` and :c:macro:`PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL` are defined:
L4582:   * If neither is defined, the C-API is declared to `static void **PyArray_API`, so it is only visible within the compilation unit/file using `#include <numpy/arrayobject.h>`.
L4583:   * If only `PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL` is defined (it could be empty) then the it is declared to a non-static `void **` allowing it to be used by other files which are linked.
L4584:   * If `NO_IMPORT_ARRAY` is defined, the table is declared as `extern void **`, meaning that it must be linked to a file which does not use `NO_IMPORT_ARRAY`.
L4585: The `PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL` mechanism additionally mangles the names to avoid conflicts.
L4586: 
L4587:     .. versionchanged::
L4588:         NumPy 2.1 changed the headers to avoid sharing the table outside of a
L4589:         single shared object/dll (this was always the case on Windows).
L4590:         Please see :c:macro:`NPY_API_SYMBOL_ATTRIBUTE` for details.
L4591: In order to make use of the C-API from another extension module, the :c:func:`import_array` function must be called. If the extension module is self-contained in a single .c file, then that is all that needs to be done. If, however, the extension module involves multiple files where the C-API is needed then some additional steps must be taken.
L4592: 
L4593:     .. c:function:: int PyArray_ImportNumPyAPI(void)
L4594: 
L4595:         Ensures that the NumPy C-API is imported and usable.  It returns ``0``
L4596:         on success and ``-1`` with an error set if NumPy couldn't be imported.
L4597:         While preferable to call it once at module initialization, this function
L4598:         is very light-weight if called multiple times.
L4599: 
L4600:         .. versionadded:: 2.0
L4601:             This function is backported in the ``npy_2_compat.h`` header.
L4602: 
L4603: 
L4604: 
L4605:     .. c:macro:: import_array(void)
L4606: 
L4607:         This function must be called in the initialization section of a
L4608:         module that will make use of the C-API. It imports the module
L4609:         where the function-pointer table is stored and points the correct
L4610:         variable to it.
L4611:         This macro includes a ``return NULL;`` on error, so that
L4612:         ``PyArray_ImportNumPyAPI()`` is preferable for custom error checking.
L4613:         You may also see use of ``_import_array()`` (a function, not
L4614:         a macro, but you may want to raise a better error if it fails) and
L4615:         the variations ``import_array1(ret)`` which customizes the return value.
L4616: 
L4617: 
L4618: 
L4619:     .. c:macro:: PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL
L4620: 
L4621: 
L4622: 
L4623:     .. c:macro:: NPY_API_SYMBOL_ATTRIBUTE
L4624: 
L4625:         .. versionadded:: 2.1
L4626: 
L4627:         An additional symbol which can be used to share e.g. visibility beyond
L4628:         shared object boundaries.
L4629:         By default, NumPy adds the C visibility hidden attribute (if available):
L4630:         ``void __attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) **PyArray_API;``.
L4631:         You can change this by defining ``NPY_API_SYMBOL_ATTRIBUTE``, which will
L4632:         make this:
L4633:         ``void NPY_API_SYMBOL_ATTRIBUTE **PyArray_API;`` (with additional
L4634:         name mangling via the unique symbol).
L4635: 
L4636:         Adding an empty ``#define NPY_API_SYMBOL_ATTRIBUTE`` will have the same
L4637:         behavior as NumPy 1.x.
L4638: 
L4639:         .. note::
L4640:             Windows never had shared visibility although you can use this macro
L4641:             to achieve it.  We generally discourage sharing beyond shared boundary
L4642:             lines since importing the array API includes NumPy version checks.
L4643: 
L4644: 
L4645: 
L4646:     .. c:macro:: NO_IMPORT_ARRAY
L4647: 
L4648:         Defining ``NO_IMPORT_ARRAY`` before the ``ndarrayobject.h`` include
L4649:         indicates that the NumPy C API import is handled in a different file
L4650:         and the include mechanism will not be added here.
L4651:         You must have one file without ``NO_IMPORT_ARRAY`` defined.
L4652:         .. code-block:: c
L4653: 
L4654:             #define PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL cool_ARRAY_API
L4655:             #include <numpy/arrayobject.h>
L4656: 
L4657:         On the other hand, coolhelper.c would contain at the top:
L4658: 
L4659:         .. code-block:: c
L4660: 
L4661:             #define NO_IMPORT_ARRAY
L4662:             #define PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL cool_ARRAY_API
L4663:             #include <numpy/arrayobject.h>
L4664: 
L4665:         You can also put the common two last lines into an extension-local
L4666:         header file as long as you make sure that NO_IMPORT_ARRAY is
L4667:         #defined before #including that file.
L4668: 
L4669:         Internally, these #defines work as follows:
L4670: 
L4671:         * If neither is defined, the C-API is declared to be
L4672:           ``static void**``, so it is only visible within the
L4673:           compilation unit that #includes numpy/arrayobject.h.
L4674:         * If :c:macro:`PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL` is #defined, but
L4675:           :c:macro:`NO_IMPORT_ARRAY` is not, the C-API is declared to
L4676:           be ``void**``, so that it will also be visible to other
L4677:           compilation units.
L4678:         * If :c:macro:`NO_IMPORT_ARRAY` is #defined, regardless of
L4679:           whether :c:macro:`PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL` is, the C-API is
L4680:           declared to be ``extern void**``, so it is expected to
L4681:           be defined in another compilation unit.
L4682:         * Whenever :c:macro:`PY_ARRAY_UNIQUE_SYMBOL` is #defined, it
L4683:           also changes the name of the variable holding the C-API, which
L4684:           defaults to ``PyArray_API``, to whatever the macro is
L4685:           #defined to.
L4686: ### Checking the API Version
L4687: 
L4688: The following definitions allow checking the NumPy compile time version, enabled C-API feature version and runtime version.
L4689: 
L4690: ABI and C-API compatibility are automatically checked when calling :c:func:`PyArray_ImportNumPyAPI` or :c:func:`import_array` and an error will be raised when these are incompatible with the NumPy runtime. User code should generally not check these manually.
L4691: For details about NumPy C-API compatibility see :ref:`for-downstream-package-authors`.
L4692: 
L4693:     .. c:macro:: NPY_VERSION
L4694: 
L4695:         The ABI version of the NumPy headers at compile time.
L4696: 
L4697: 
L4698: 
L4699:     .. c:macro:: NPY_FEATURE_VERSION
L4700: 
L4701:         The version of the NumPy C-API the compilation targets.
L4702:         Setting ``NPY_TARGET_VERSION`` may modify this value to make newer
L4703:         NumPy API features available or, in principle, to be compatible with
L4704:         older NumPy versions.
L4705:     .. c:macro:: PyArray_RUNTIME_VERSION
L4706: 
L4707:         After the C-API has been imported ``PyArray_RUNTIME_VERSION`` is set to
L4708:         the current runtime C-API version. ``PyArray_RUNTIME_VERSION`` is
L4709:         mainly used when necessary to support both old and new NumPy versions.
L4710: 
L4711: 
L4712: 
L4713:     .. c:function:: unsigned int PyArray_GetNDArrayCVersion(void)
L4714: 
L4715:         This just returns the value :c:data:`NPY_VERSION`. :c:data:`NPY_VERSION`
L4716:         changes whenever a backward incompatible change at the ABI level. Because
L4717:         it is in the C-API, however, comparing the output of this function from the
L4718:         value defined in the current header gives a way to test if the C-API has
L4719:         changed thus requiring a re-compilation of extension modules that use the
L4720:         C-API. This is automatically checked in the function :c:func:`import_array`.
L4721: 
L4722: 
L4723: 
L4724:     .. c:function:: unsigned int PyArray_GetNDArrayCFeatureVersion(void)
L4725:         This just returns the value :c:data:`NPY_FEATURE_VERSION`.
L4726:         :c:data:`NPY_FEATURE_VERSION` changes whenever the API changes (e.g. a
L4727:         function is added). A changed value does not always require a recompile.

L4793: ### Threading support
L4794: These macros are only meaningful if :c:data:`NPY_ALLOW_THREADS` evaluates True during compilation of the extension module. Otherwise, these macros are equivalent to whitespace. Python uses a single Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) for each Python process so that only a single thread may execute at a time (even on multi-cpu machines).
